theater: 敘利亞北境至幼發拉底河

battle.name: 第七次敘利亞戰役
battle.theater: 敘利亞北境至幼發拉底河
battle.brief: 前1448年，新王國法老圖特摩斯三世再舉兵北向，擊破米坦尼聯盟在敘利亞諸邦的抵抗，戰線自奧龍特斯河一路推到幼發拉底河畔的卡爾凱美什與埃馬爾，迫使「大王」納貢稱臣。埃及步兵手持月牙形青銅短劍近身格鬥，弓手列陣射擊，戰車與輜重隊沿奧龍特斯谷地北進，是這場戰役的骨幹。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 交戰的兩方是埃及新王國第十八王朝與以胡里人為核心的米坦尼聯盟。埃及方面由法老圖特摩斯三世親任最高統帥，國王自帶近衛與王牌弓手隊出戰，軍隊骨架是步兵：中央是配圓盾、長柄銅斧與短矛的重裝步兵，兩翼與前鋒是數量最多的埃及弓手，另有數百輛至數千輛雙輪戰車留作突擊與追擊；傭兵與徵召兵中還有來自黎凡特、努比亞與西部沙漠的謝爾登人、麥傑人與沙漠部族，軍需由軍中文書記錄口糧配給與徵發物資。米坦尼方面是上美索不達米亞的胡里王國，國王自稱「大王」，都城瓦舒卡尼在今日土耳其與敘利亞邊境一帶，位置至今未能確定；大王以宗主身分控制敘利亞諸邦——卡脫納、圖尼普、阿勒頗、比布魯斯與西頓——以及幼發拉底河中游的卡爾凱美什、埃馬爾等城，聯軍以步兵、車兵與胡里弓手為骨幹。赫梯此時仍據安納托利亞高原，尚未南下爭奪敘利亞，與本戰役只有間接關係；真正左右物資流向的是巴比倫：青金石自巴比倫經米坦尼一線轉往埃及，這條商路的控制權正是大王不肯輕易讓步的緣由之一。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were Egypt of the Eighteenth Dynasty and the Mitanni coalition built around Hurrian power. On the Egyptian side the supreme commander was the pharaoh Thutmose III, who led the host in person, taking the royal guard and the elite corps of bowmen with him; the framework of the army was infantry: heavy foot with round shields, long-handled bronze axes and short spears in the centre, Egyptian archers — the largest contingent — on the wings and in the vanguard, and between several hundred and several thousand two-wheeled chariots held back for breakthrough and pursuit; mercenaries and conscripts included Sherden, Medjay and desert tribes from the Levant, Nubia and the western oases, while army scribes kept ration tallies and requisition lists. On the Mitanni side stood the Hurrian kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia, whose king called himself the Great King and whose capital, Washukanni, lay somewhere on the border between modern Turkey and Syria and has never been located with certainty; the Great King held the Syrian city-states — Qatna, Tunip, Aleppo, Byblos and Sidon — as his own vassals, together with Carchemish and Emar on the middle Euphrates, and his coalition fought with infantry, chariot troops and Hurrian archers. The Hittites at this date still held the Anatolian plateau and had not yet come south to contest Syria, so their part in this war is indirect; what really governed the flow of goods was Babylon, because lapis lazuli travelled from Babylon through Mitanni to Egypt, and control of that trade route was one of the things the Great King would not lightly surrender.
people: 核心人物是埃及法老圖特摩斯三世（Menkheperre）。他在位約三十八年，執政前期已以北方遠征立威，這場戰役是他統治中期的又一次大規模北征：國王本人統率全軍，並非坐鎮後方，日常指揮由宰相（Vizier）與「弓箭手隊長」一類的軍職分擔，軍中文書更留下逐日行程與地名清單，後人才能循名單還原路線。對面的米坦尼之主是自稱「大王」的胡里君主，具體人名在不同文獻中排序不一，一般認為是圖特基什一系，其後才是前1400年代在阿瑪納字母中與埃及通信的圖胥拉塔。敘利亞方面，阿勒頗一系的王公與卡脫納、圖尼普的統治者是各自與大王結盟的城邦領袖，其中阿勒頗之王的名號在埃及文獻中拼法不一，連是不是同一人都有爭議。戰後的外交主角則轉到米坦尼：圖胥拉塔在阿門霍特普三世治下屢次致書埃及索取銀兩、乞求一尊自己的雕像，甚至把自己的女兒送進埃及宮中；巴比倫王布爾納布里什一世寫給埃及王的信大意是祝賀埃及攻入米坦尼，並提到米坦尼王族有子弟長駐埃及——這些信件讓「大王」的處境第一次留下當事人自己的說法，而不再只是埃及年表上的勝利宣告。
peopleEn: The central figure is the Egyptian pharaoh Thutmose III (Menkheperre). He reigned for about thirty-eight years and had already made his name in the north with an early expedition, so this war was another large northern campaign of the middle part of his reign: the king commanded the host in person rather than directing it from the rear, with day-to-day control delegated to the vizier and to offices such as the chief of the bowmen, while army scribes drew up day-by-day itineraries and place-name lists, which is how the route can be reconstructed at all today. The opposing ruler of Mitanni was the Hurrian monarch who styled himself the Great King; his personal name is ordered differently in different documents, and he is generally placed in the line of Tutkigsh, with Tushratta — the king who corresponded with Egypt in the Amarna letters of the fifteenth century — coming after him. On the Syrian side, the dynast of the Aleppo line and the rulers of Qatna and Tunip were city-state leaders, each of them allied with the Great King; even the name of the king of Aleppo varies in Egyptian sources, and whether the references point to one man or more than one is disputed. The diplomatic protagonist of the aftermath shifts to Mitanni: Tushratta wrote to Egypt repeatedly under Amenhotep III asking for silver, begging for a statue of himself, and even sent his own daughter into the Egyptian court; and a letter from Burnaburiash I of Babylon to the king of Egypt congratulates him, in substance, on having taken ground in Mitanni, and mentions that a member of the Mitanni royal house was staying at the Egyptian court. These letters are the first time the Great King's predicament is described in the words of the parties themselves, and no longer only as a victory proclamation in an Egyptian chronicle.
kits: 本卡兵器是埃及月牙劍：內彎的單刃青銅短劍，形制源於中期王朝的鵝嘴斧，第二中間期已出現在實戰裝備中，新王國初期成為埃及近戰步兵的標準配備。刃口向內彎，砍入甲胄或人體後不必把劍拔出來，可以連砍帶拉地撕開傷口，因此又被說成「砍下去不用拔」；它配的是小型圓盾（卡普盾）與一把直刃短匕，弓手之外的近戰步兵則以它對付失去衝力的散兵。劍身為銅或青銅，比後來的直刃青銅劍短而重，穿透鎧甲的能力有限，遇到鱗甲往往只能砍、拖、擲，全靠力氣與手位取勝，這也是它要配短匕而非獨力破甲的原因。埃及步兵整體裝備還包括角、筋、木製的複合弓，弓手是軍隊中數量最多的一環，箭簇以燙硬打製；近戰兵另有長柄銅斧、標槍與短矛。車兵是突破與追擊的力量：木輪雙輪車，自圖特摩斯三世起四匹馬挽的車漸多，御者與射手同車，負責掩護弓手陣線、擴開缺口。攻城方面，埃及兵備有圍城用的攻城塔、撞錘與填土斜坡，並以弓手與標槍先壓制城頭；後來底比斯一處軍人墓的壁畫，仍以雲梯與攻城柱描繪埃及人攻打敘利亞堡壘的樣子。與此同時，雙方的主要遠程火力仍是弓：胡里與敘利亞弓手用複合弓，聯軍的近戰則以銅斧與雙刃斧為主。補給靠驢騾隊與牛車運糧，以及城邦徵發的穀物、葡萄酒與金屬；銅來自西奈與亞洲，錫與青金石則經巴比倫方向運來。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Egyptian khopesh: a short bronze sword with an inward-curving single edge, a form descended from the duckbill axe of the Middle Kingdom, already appearing in field service in the Second Intermediate Period and standard equipment for Egyptian close-combat infantry in the early New Kingdom. Because the edge curves inward, the blade can be driven in and pulled without being withdrawn — the cut is made by tearing as much as by chopping — and this is what the saying about not needing to pull the sword back out refers to. It was carried with a small round shield, the kappu, and with a straight-edged dagger, and the close-combat foot behind the archers used it against troops whose momentum had been broken. The blade was copper or bronze, shorter and heavier than the straight-edged bronze swords that came later, and poor at penetrating armour; against scale protection it could only chop, drag and throw, and everything depended on strength and the angle of the wrist, which is precisely why it was paired with a dagger rather than expected to break armour on its own. The rest of the Egyptian infantry loadout included composite bows of horn, sinew and wood, and the archers were the largest single contingent in the army, their arrowheads hardened in fire; the close-combat foot also carried long-handled bronze axes, javelins and short spears. Chariotry was the force for breakthrough and pursuit: two-wheeled cars of wood, with four-horse teams becoming commoner from the time of Thutmose III, the driver and the archer riding together, their business being to cover the archers' line and to open the gaps. For siege work the Egyptians had towers, battering rams and earth ramps, and they cleared the wall with arrows and javelins before the assault; a later tomb of a soldier at Thebes still shows Egyptian troops assaulting a Syrian fortress with ladders and a siege tower. Meanwhile the principal long-range weapon on both sides remained the bow: Hurrian and Syrian archers used composite bows, and the coalition's close combat turned on bronze axes and double-bit axes. Supply came up with donkey and mule trains and ox carts carrying grain, together with the requisitioned grain, wine and metal of the city-states; the copper came from Sinai and from Asia, while tin and lapis lazuli arrived by way of Babylon.
tactics: 埃及的遠征有一套固定做法：軍隊不整隊行軍，而分成數路縱隊推進——中央縱隊沿大道走，左翼沿奧龍特斯河谷作先鋒，右翼貼近海岸與山麓作掩護，三路在會合處同時壓上；沿途每日宿營前派出偵察，軍中文書把道路、村落與渡口記在行程表上，後人甚至能從殘存的「地名表」裡還原行軍路線。渡過幼發拉底河是全戰最要緊的一步：河上沒有橋，須以船、筏或浮橋分批渡過，埃及人甚至先造好船、把船由海路運到陸路再搬過陸地，以便從北岸登船，渡口一旦被守，遠征即告中止；渡河之後大軍立刻圍城或設營，把城內的水井與耕地控制在自己手裡。會戰陣形以步兵正面與弓手在兩翼展開，戰車不放在前線，而是留待敵陣出現缺口時一齊投入，衝開之後才讓步兵帶月牙劍湧入缺口作近身砍殺。攻城多以圍而不打與突擊並用：先用弓手與標槍清理城頭，再以雲梯攀城或斷糧迫降，必要時堆土築斜坡，把車兵送上城牆高度。外交與戰爭並行：對敘利亞城邦用「宗主—納貢」收編，對「大王」則以軍威迫其送來黃金與青金石，甚至索取條約副本與結盟印璽，把戰場上的結果直接換算成外交上的收益。
tacticsEn: The Egyptians had a settled method for a distant campaign. The army did not march as one column: it advanced in several parallel columns, the central one on the main road, the left wing through the valley of the Orontes as the vanguard, the right wing close to the coast and the foothills as cover, the three closing together at a point of rendezvous. Scouting parties went out before each night's halt, and army scribes entered roads, villages and fords in the itinerary, so that the line of march can be reconstructed from a surviving topographical list of place names. The crossing of the Euphrates was the most critical step of the whole war: there were no bridges, the host had to be ferried across in boats, rafts or pontoons, and the Egyptians even had ships built and then carried overland by portage so that they could board from the northern bank; if the fords were held the expedition was over. Once across, the army at once invested the city or entrenched, taking control of the wells and the fields inside it. In pitched battle the line was infantry frontally with archers on the wings; the chariots were not committed to the front but were held back and launched together when a gap opened in the enemy formation, and only then did the infantry with their khopesh pour through the gap and finish the business at close quarters. Sieges combined blockade with sudden assault: the wall was first cleared with arrows and javelins, then scaled with ladders or reduced by starvation, and where necessary earth was tipped up into a ramp to bring the chariots to the height of the rampart. Diplomacy ran alongside the war: the Syrian city-states were folded into a system of overlordship and tribute, while the Great King was pressed by force of arms to send gold and lapis lazuli, and even to hand over a copy of a treaty and a seal of alliance, so that what was won on the field was converted directly into diplomatic gain.
data: 可核對的數字如下。年代通常記作前1448年，它對應到圖特摩斯三世統治中後期那幾次直抵幼發拉底河的北征之一，具體年份有前1446年、前1438年前後等不同說法；圖特摩斯三世在位約三十八年，約前1479年至前1425年。距離方面，敘利亞境內由比布魯斯到阿勒頗約二百五十公里，阿勒頗到幼發拉底河畔的卡爾凱美什不足一百公里，由卡脫納到卡爾凱美什約一百六十公里；一日行程一般二十至三十公里，故單由比布魯斯打到幼發拉底河，純行軍就要十至十五日，遠征全程遠超此數。兵力方面，埃及方面的核心步兵一般估計在數千至一萬之間，弓手占其中多數，戰車常在數百輛的量級，部分估算高至數千輛；對面聯軍靠各城邦拼湊，總數亦在數千至一萬上下，車兵比例低於埃及。物資來源同樣可查：埃及從西奈的塞伊納等銅礦取銅，從巴比倫方向取得青金石，而銅與青金石多經米坦尼一線轉運，這說明商路正是爭端所在；另從黎巴嫩海岸運雪松木入埃及，在新王國盛期達到高峰。戰果數字須打折扣：埃及碑文以擄獲人數、馬匹與金銀器計功，數量常被後世學者調低數倍，宜視為宣傳量度而非統計。最硬的證據是阿瑪納字母：現存約三百五十封，其中逾二百封涉及米坦尼。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run as follows. The date is normally given as 1448 BC, and the war is tied to one of the late campaigns in which Thutmose III drove his army up to the Euphrates; the exact year is given variously as 1446 BC or around 1438 BC. Thutmose III reigned about thirty-eight years, roughly from 1479 to 1425 BC. As for distances: within Syria the run from Byblos to Aleppo is about two hundred and fifty kilometres, from Aleppo to Carchemish on the Euphrates rather less than a hundred, and from Qatna to Carchemish about a hundred and sixty; a day's march was generally twenty to thirty kilometres, so marching from Byblos to the Euphrates alone took ten to fifteen days, and the full expedition was far longer. On numbers of men: the Egyptian core infantry is generally estimated at several thousand up to ten thousand, with archers forming the majority of it, and chariots usually counted in the hundreds, though some estimates run to several thousand; the opposing coalition was assembled from the several city-states and came to a comparable several thousand up to ten thousand, with a lower proportion of chariot troops. The flow of supplies can be traced just as well: Egypt drew copper from the mines of Sinai such as Timna, and lapis lazuli from the Babylonian direction, and both moved largely through the Mitanni line, which shows that the trade route was precisely what was at issue; and cedar timber shipped from the Levantine coast into Egypt reached a peak in the high period of the New Kingdom. Capture figures have to be discounted: Egyptian monuments count the enemy dead and taken, the horses and the metalware, and later scholars routinely cut those numbers by a factor of several, so they are better read as propaganda measures than as statistics. The hardest evidence of all is the Amarna correspondence: about three hundred and fifty letters survive, of which more than two hundred concern Mitanni.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最外層是地理與商路：埃及要保住從西奈運出的銅礦、從黎巴嫩運入的雪松木，以及由巴比倫方向經米坦尼轉入的青金石，這條商路一旦被截斷，新王國的財政與神廟工程都要停滯；更關鍵的是幼發拉底河中游的卡爾凱美什與埃馬爾控制了從上游運銅、鉛、錫下行的通道，誰占住那兩城，誰就捏住幼發拉底河兩岸的關稅與人頭稅。中層是宗主權之爭：米坦尼大王在西屬的敘利亞諸邦面前自居宗主，埃及則要否認這層宗主關係，寧可自己收編卡脫納、圖尼普與阿勒頗。最內層是政治：圖特摩斯三世早年在宮中經歷繼承風波，成年後需要北方戰功來鞏固王位與一批有戰功的將領，敘利亞戰事既可收回邊境要塞，也能餵養軍功集團。戰前數年，敘利亞方面的摩擦加劇：城邦聯軍在北境收緊對埃及商隊的封鎖，埃及在基列與比布魯斯的據點遭到襲擾，圖特摩斯三世遂以此為口實，於春末夏初舉兵北上，把一次邊界衝突擴成了一場直取幼發拉底河的遠征。
causeEn: The war began for three layers of reason. The outermost was geography and trade: Egypt had to keep the copper coming down from Sinai, the cedar coming in from the Levant, and the lapis lazuli coming through Mitanni from Babylon, and if that route were cut the finances and the temple works of the New Kingdom would all stall. More decisively, Carchemish and Emar on the middle Euphrates controlled the passages down which copper, lead and tin moved from the upper reaches; whoever held those two cities held the tolls and the head-counts of both banks of the river. The middle layer was a struggle over overlordship: the Great King of Mitanni claimed the Syrian city-states as his own subordinates, while Egypt denied him that claim and preferred to take Qatna, Tunip and Aleppo into its own hand. The innermost layer was political: Thutmose III had been through a disputed succession in the palace as a youth, and once grown he needed northern victories to shore up his throne and to reward a circle of commanders; a Syrian war would recover the frontier fortresses and feed that circle. In the years before the campaign friction rose: the coalition tightened its stranglehold on Egyptian caravans in the north, and Egyptian posts in Gilead and Byblos came under harassment, and Thutmose III took this as his warrant, marching north in the last month of spring and turning a border clash into an expedition aimed at the Euphrates.
impact: 對埃及，這場戰役把新王國的亞洲政策推到頂點。敘利亞自此進入埃及的宗主體系：卡脫納、圖尼普、比布魯斯、西頓與阿勒頗按年進貢金、銀、鉛、錫、銅、象牙、馬匹、葡萄酒、食用油與人丁；埃及在本地設官徵收，敘利亞的葡萄酒與黎巴嫩雪松大量運入三角洲，神廟與船塢的建材因此不斷。對米坦尼，這是一場結構性挫敗：大王的西屬地盤幾乎被逐出幼發拉底河以西，王室退守上美索不達米亞，前1400年代起只能靠外交求生——向埃及借銀、乞求一尊自己的雕像、把自己的女兒送進埃及宮廷，甚至一度試圖與埃及王室結親。更遠地看，這條路也通向後來兩大強權在幼發拉底河上游的角力：前1400年代赫梯自安納托利亞南下，前13世紀埃及拉美西斯二世與赫梯王穆瓦塔里二世在卡爾凱美什會戰，讓這座城再次成為前線；而阿瑪納字母因記錄了米坦尼的求饒與兩國彼此試探，也成了後世重建青銅時代國際外交的第一手材料。
impactEn: For Egypt the war carried the Asian policy of the New Kingdom to its high point. Syria entered the Egyptian system of overlordship: Qatna, Tunip, Byblos, Sidon and Aleppo paid annual tribute in gold, silver, lead, tin, copper, ivory, horses, wine, oil and labour; Egypt stationed officials to collect it, and the wine of Syria and the cedar of the Levant poured into the Delta, feeding temple and dockyard building without end. For Mitanni this was a structural defeat: the Great King's western holdings were driven back almost entirely from the far side of the Euphrates, the royal house withdrew to Upper Mesopotamia, and from the fifteenth century onward it could survive only by diplomacy — borrowing silver from Egypt, begging for a statue of itself, sending its own daughter into the Egyptian court, and at one point attempting a marriage alliance with the Egyptian royal house. Looking further ahead, the road ran on to the rivalry of the two great powers over the upper Euphrates: the Hittites came south out of Anatolia in the fifteenth century, and in the thirteenth century Ramses II of Egypt and the Hittite king Muwatalli II met at Carchemish, putting that city back on the frontier. And because the Amarna letters record Mitanni's supplication and the mutual testing of the two courts, they remain the primary document for reconstructing Bronze Age international diplomacy.
result: 結果是埃及以野戰勝利換來政治上限：敘利亞諸邦臣服於埃及宗主權之下，幼發拉底河成為埃及在北部的實際邊界，遠征的實際收穫不是佔土，而是名分與貢賦；大王一方雖未覆亡，仍保有「大王」名號與上美索不達米亞的核心地盤，往後數十年靠書信周旋，把國家拖到阿瑪納時代那種仰賴埃及援助的處境。若要說勝負怎樣算，埃及贏了戰役卻沒有贏下北界：它無法在幼發拉底河以北常駐軍隊，影響仍要靠一次次重兵出動維持。至於這場戰役在編年上的位置，多數學者依馬奈托留下的戰爭計數與現代學者肯尼斯·基欽的重建，把它放在前1440年代中葉圖特摩斯三世的一次北征，稱為第七次敘利亞戰役；也有學者把編號往前挪，視前1457年美吉多之戰為第六、這次遠征為第七，或把「大王」受制於埃及的那段稱為第八次。今天能確認的細節有限，戰役過程多靠卡爾納克年表的殘片、軍隊地名表與阿瑪納字母拼回，月牙劍手的近身格鬥、弓手在會戰兩翼的箭雨與渡河後的圍城，是這場戰爭留給後世最清晰的畫面。
resultEn: The outcome was an Egyptian tactical victory exchanged for a political ceiling: the Syrian city-states became subjects of Egyptian overlordship and the Euphrates became Egypt's effective northern frontier, so what the expedition actually bought was recognition and tribute rather than territory. The Great King's state was not destroyed; it kept the title of Great King and the core of Upper Mesopotamia, and for decades turned to correspondence to hold the realm together, until it reached the position in the Amarna age of depending on Egyptian help. As for the arithmetic of the result: Egypt won the campaign but did not win the northern border, for it could not keep an army stationed beyond the Euphrates, and its influence had to be maintained by dispatching heavy columns again and again. As for where the war sits in the chronology, most scholars follow the count of campaigns preserved by Manetho and the reconstruction of the modern historian Kenneth Kitchen, and place it in the northern expedition of Thutmose III in the middle of the fifteenth century, calling it the Seventh Syrian War; others shift the numbering, taking the battle of Megiddo in 1457 BC as the sixth and this expedition as the seventh, or naming the period in which the Great King was at Egypt's mercy as the eighth. The details that can be confirmed today are few, and the course of the war has to be pieced together from the fragments of the Karnak annals, the army's topographical list and the Amarna letters; the khopesh fighter at close quarters, the arrow-fall from the archers on the wings of a pitched battle, and the siege that followed the crossing of the river are the clearest pictures the war has left behind.
